PullRequest.Title: editor: Balance auto-closing brackets
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #6841

# Summary

- Keeps auto-closing brackets balanced when an opening bracket is typed before a matching unmatched closer later in the document, avoiding a duplicate closing bracket.
- Adds token- and language-aware unmatched-closer detection so brackets in strings, comments, and embedded languages do not affect the decision.

# Known Limitations

- The balancing check is skipped until token-aware bracket data is available and for documents too large for the bracket-pair AST. These cases retain the existing auto-closing behavior.
- Multi-cursor typing uses a shared auto-closing decision. If any cursor can reuse a later unmatched closer, auto-closing is suppressed for the entire edit.
- `editor.autoClosingBrackets: "always"` continues to insert a closing bracket unconditionally by design. Quote auto-closing is unchanged.

# Manual checklist

- [x] In a JSON or JSONC document, remove an opening `{` while leaving its matching `}` later in the document, then retype `{` and verify that no duplicate `}` is inserted.
- [x] In an empty document, type `{`, `[`, and `(` and verify that each still inserts its matching closer.
- [x] Put a non-matching closer after the cursor, type an opening bracket, and verify that its matching closer is still inserted.
- [x] Verify that bracket characters inside strings, comments, and an embedded-language region do not suppress normal auto-closing.
- [x] Repeat the unmatched-closer scenario with multiple cursors and verify the shared auto-closing behavior described above.
- [x] Set `editor.autoClosingBrackets` to `always` and verify that typing an opener always inserts its closer.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The input call path is direct, the tree's lazy-construction guard and 5,000,000-character limit are explicit, and BracketPairsTree's constructor calls parseDocument over the text buffer when the tree is absent. The disabled colorization provider returns without requesting brackets and bracket guides default off, establishing a realistic cold-tree state. Exact pause duration varies by document and hardware.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread document token scanning, AST node allocations, and retained bracket-tree objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold cost grows linearly with document text/tokens and bracket count, up to the 5,000,000-character AST cutoff. It occurs once per cold model; warm calls avoid rebuilding the whole tree, while multi-cursor typing adds one query per cursor after that initial build.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked input critical path with CPU/allocation pressure and retained model memory
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Auto-closing decisions did not request the bracket-pair AST. When colorization was disabled and guides were off, typing an opener left the lazy tree unbuilt and performed only the existing local line/token checks.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: An opening-bracket keystroke now requests the bracket-pair tree. On a cold model this synchronously tokenizes/parses the entire document into an AST and retains it, before the query can decide whether token-aware data is usable.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side call at cursorTypeEditOperations.ts:253 invokes hasUnmatchedClosingBracketAfter from the opener-typing loop. That new API sets bracketsRequested=true and calls updateBracketPairsTree before testing token accuracy; when no tree exists, updateBracketPairsTree constructs BracketPairsTree synchronously for every model up to 5,000,000 characters.
Findings.Title: Avoid building the whole bracket AST on an opener keystroke
Findings.Impact: With bracket-pair colorization/guides disabled (or another editor/model where no bracket consumer has run), the first `{`, `[`, or `(` in a multi-megabyte file can pause typing while up to 5 MB is parsed and a proportional AST is allocated and retained. This defeats the responsiveness benefit of disabling bracket visualization; the waste is especially clear while background tokenization is incomplete because the result is not used.
Findings.Evidence: AutoClosingOpenCharTypeOperation calls the query synchronously while producing edits. BracketPairsTextModelPart.hasUnmatchedClosingBracketAfter sets bracketsRequested and calls updateBracketPairsTree; updateBracketPairsTree creates BracketPairsTree when absent for documents <= 50,000*100 characters. Its constructor parses the text buffer with parseDocumentFromTextBuffer/FastTokenizer, whose parser walks tokens and constructs AST nodes. Only after this construction does BracketPairsTree.hasUnmatchedClosingBracketAfter check hasAccurateTokensForLine(lastLine) and potentially return false. ColorizedBracketPairsDecorationProvider does not request the tree when colorization is disabled, and bracket guides default to false.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep whole-document tree creation off the keystroke path: query only an already-available token-aware tree and schedule/build it outside input handling, or at least check full-model token accuracy and tree availability before setting bracketsRequested/updateBracketPairsTree so an unusable AST is not constructed synchronously.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type the first auto-closing bracket in a cold model with bracket-pair colorization and guides disabled, especially while background tokenization is incomplete.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AutoClosingOpenCharTypeOperation.getAutoClosingPairClose runs synchronously before producing the typing edit. The bracket-tree construction and query must finish before the typed character is applied.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Document text/token/bracket count controls the cold O(document) parse and retained AST size; selection count controls warm query multiplicity after effective sharing of the single tree build.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is synchronous and serialized on the editor/main-thread input path. A cold multi-cursor edit performs one initial tree build, followed by sequential position queries until one returns true or all cursors are checked.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold models with no prior bracket consumer have no BracketPairsTree. The first eligible opener builds and retains one; later opener checks reuse it but flush queued edits synchronously. If tokenization is incomplete, the cold build still occurs before the query returns false. Models over the 5,000,000-character AST cutoff do not build it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added keystroke call directly reaches lazy tree construction, whose constructor performs a full text-buffer parse before token-accuracy gating.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact parse latency and the prevalence of large models with colorization disabled vary by hardware and settings; the synchronous full-document work and 5,000,000-character upper bound are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff moves whole-document AST construction and retention onto the input critical path, and can do that work even when the new semantic check cannot use it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type an opener in a normally rendered editor where the bracket AST is already warm, including multi-cursor edits.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new query and any queued incremental parse complete synchronously before the opener edit. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of cursor positions checked, with a balanced 2-3 AST and missing-bracket metadata pruning traversal by position and bracket kind.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sequential on the editor thread. Multi-cursor typing invokes one query per cursor and short-circuits at the first unmatched closer; no parallelism or coalescing across positions beyond sharing the tree.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing tree is warm because default bracket-pair colorization or another bracket consumer requested it. Queued content/token edits are lazily applied by flushQueue before the query; subsequent calls reuse the updated tree.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability and per-cursor query multiplicity; insufficient evidence that the pruned AST traversal or incremental flush is independently expensive enough to report.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Incremental reparse cost depends on pending edits and bracket structure, but repository code is designed to reuse unaffected AST nodes; no high-confidence document-wide repeated-work regression was established for the warm path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the query is synchronous and repeated per cursor, but metadata pruning and AST reuse prevent proving a realistic high-impact scaling regression distinct from the cold build.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type quotes, use unconditional bracket auto-closing, complete composition, or edit a document above the bracket-AST cutoff.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These guards complete before the new balance query, so the changed AST work is off the path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Not applicable after the guard; no changed collection or boundary multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous typing handling only; no new concurrency or boundary behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No bracket-balance cache/tree access occurs for quotes, `autoClosingBrackets: always`, composition-end paths where the character is already present, non-auto-closing characters, or models beyond the AST size cutoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the explicit conditions surrounding the added call and canBuildAST guard.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the performance pass because the changed expensive work is gated out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression from the changed balance query because these paths skip it or skip AST construction.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced opener typing through lazy bracket-tree ownership, parser/tokenization work, warm incremental updates, multi-cursor multiplicity, tokenization gating, configuration defaults, and all changed/transitive expensive boundaries. Submitted one medium-severity eager-work finding for cold whole-document AST construction on the input path; no concrete subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out was introduced, and no shipped performance-regression fix was established.
